learning_outcomes.text: Understand the fundamentals and basic applications of heat transfer and Fluid Mechanics, their laws and principles, knowing how to apply them to practical situations in industry and other economic sectors, with quality, safety, efficiency, and good judgment, using the minimum possible resources.
Understand, master, and apply all thermofluid dynamic concepts for the design of heat exchangers in industry and other sectors.
Solve problems and practical situations concerning various refrigeration and heating processes, seeking their optimization and adaptation to the most common real situations.

Have a solid foundation to adapt knowledge and its applications to subsequent applications of thermal machines and installations and to positively acquire later concepts of the degree in the field of Thermal and Fluid Engineering.
Ability to apply knowledge to practice.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Knowledge of applied thermodynamics and heat transfer. Basic principles and their application to solving engineering problems.

syllabus_topics: Heat Transfer by Conduction - Introduction to heat transfer - Fourier's Law - Application of Fourier's Law
Heat Transfer by Convection - Introduction - Newton's Law - Dimensional analysis - Natural and forced convection
Heat Transfer by Radiation - Introduction - Irradiation - Laws of radiation - Radiosity
Mixed Heat Transfer - Introduction - Newton's Law of Cooling - Basic cases
Heat Exchangers - Introduction - Analysis of heat exchangers
Power Cycles - Rankine Cycle - Otto Cycle - Diesel Cycle - Brayton Cycle
Refrigeration Cycles - Introduction - Classification - Vapor compression refrigeration cycle - Calculation procedure - Low temperature refrigeration production
Refrigeration Technology - Compressor - Condenser - Evaporator - Expansion valve - Other elements
Psychrometry and Air Conditioning - Introduction - Psychrometric processes - Air conditioning cycles - Equipment selection - Selection of the appropriate system
Practical sessions - Problem-solving for Power Cycles using the EES program - Tutored work on practical applications of Thermal Engineering Fundamentals in a multi-family residential building
assessment_rules: A minimum of 35% of the total score from written exams must be obtained. If this critical assessment criterion is not met, the final grade for the course will be 'FAIL', with the resulting score from the sum of all evaluation systems, truncated to a maximum of 4.5 points.
